candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71) (c. 100 BC)

'And the spirit translated Enoch to the heaven of heavens, and I saw there as it were a structure built of crystals, and between those crystals tongues of living fire' — the crystal-and-fire heavenly architecture (parallel to Rev 4:6 sea-of-glass and Rev 21:18-21 crystal city walls). Tewahedo architectural symbolism (the use of polished stone and white-glazed surfaces in Lalibela's monolithic churches) draws on this Enochic vision-architecture as canonical aesthetic.

candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71) (c. 100 BC)

'And I fell on my face, and my whole body became relaxed, and my spirit was transfigured; and I cried with a loud voice... with the spirit of power, and blessed and glorified and extolled' — Enoch's transfiguration. Tewahedo mystical theology reads this verse as a pre-Christian witness to the deification (theosis) tradition: the human person can be transfigured in body and spirit through divine encounter. The Tewahedo monastic feast of Mount Tabor draws explicit liturgical parallels between Christ's Transfiguration and Enoch's, using 71:11 as a reading.

candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71) (c. 100 BC)

'Thou art the Son of Man who art born unto righteousness, and righteousness abides over thee, and the righteousness of the Head of Days forsakes thee not' — the controversial closing of the Parables where Enoch himself is identified WITH the Son of Man. Charles' translation preserves this identification; some scholars argue for an alternative reading. The Tewahedo reception holds the text as it stands: Enoch's eschatological exaltation to the role of Son of Man does NOT compete with later Christological identification but anticipates it — Enoch is a TYPE of the Son of Man whose fullness is Christ. This typological reading is preserved in the Mäṣḥafä Hēnok's catechetical use within the Tewahedo monastic tradition.
